conviction_note: Scale is the 9.0% event-implied move nudged to 9.5 because a Q4 guide sits in this release and the name's own median reaction is 7.3%. p_up is 45, a slight lean down: five of the last six prints were sold; the dollar has strengthened since the July guide; and the CEO said on record on Oct 1 that growth is slower than he wants. Against that, the stock is 4% off its 52-week low with price targets already cut and the skew mildly upside-paid, so the lean stays small. The findings sum to -0.7 and the scaled number is -0.95; both are small and they agree in sign.
bar: Q3 2026: company guide revenue $12.86bn, op margin 33.2%, diluted EPS $0.82 (shareholder letter, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065280/000106528026000211/ex991_q226.htm). Street consensus revenue $12.87-12.88bn, EPS $0.82: Hudson Labs ($12,879M, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/netflix-q3-2026-earnings-preview-nflx-revenue-guidance), Finbold ($12.87bn / $0.82, https://finbold.com/traders-predict-netflixs-next-direction-after-tomorrows-earnings-release/) and Zacks via AAII. Benzinga/Reuters show $0.84 / $13.0bn, so the EPS bar is slightly disputed. The Q3 bar is sourced and sits on the guide. Q4 2026 is the line the stock trades on. No Q4 consensus was found. The FY guide of $51.0-51.4bn less Q1 $12.25bn, Q2 $12.56bn and Q3 guide $12.86bn implies Q4 revenue of $13.33-13.73bn (+10.6% to +13.9% on Q4'25's $12.05bn). The FY 31.5% margin target implies a Q4 op margin of about 27.7%. Because the Q4 bar is unsourced, the guidance findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is not crowded. Equibles shows about 81M shares short at the 2026-03-13 settlement, 1.73 days to cover, about 2% of roughly 4.2bn post-split shares (https://equibles.com/stocks/nflx/shortinterest). No October 2026 figure was found. 25-delta skew is -2.07 vol points (upside paid) and put/call OI is 0.63, so the option market leans mildly up. Polymarket on Oct 19 put 68% on a close above $70 for the week ending Oct 23 against a $69.83 spot (https://finbold.com/traders-predict-netflixs-next-direction-after-tomorrows-earnings-release/). Run-up is -3.2% over 20 days, -44% from the 52-week high and +4% from the 52-week low ($65.08, set after July's print). Analyst stance turned bearish into the print: Wells Fargo Underweight $57 (Sep 18), HSBC to Hold $76 (Sep 22), Huber Sell $70, BMO PT $135 to $125, Wedbush $105 to $90.

findings.finding: The CEO said on record that growth is slower than he wants, and Netflix then replaced its content chief. At Bloomberg Screentime on 2026-10-01 co-CEO Ted Sarandos said 'we're not growing as fast as I want us to'. On 2026-10-15 Netflix announced that CCO Bela Bajaria is out and ex-Disney Peter Rice starts 2026-10-26. Together these suggest the Q4 guide and the letter's engagement commentary are more likely to disappoint than to surprise up. The bar is the implied Q4 revenue of $13.33-13.73bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The forward guide moved the last three prints. A Q3 guide below the street took the stock -7.26% on 2026-07-16 despite a small beat. The Apr-2026 print fell -9.72% and Oct-2025 fell -10.07%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell into early October and Wells Fargo said the remarks raise questions on Q3 and 2027. But the stock rose 2.9% on 2026-10-15, the CCO-change day, so the market read the change as a fix rather than as a warning on the outlook. If the market had priced a Q4 guide cut, the skew would be put-paid, not -2.07, and Polymarket would not put 68% on a close above $70.
findings.independence: The CCO change is a separate source (https://thedesk.net/2026/10/netflix-replaces-bela-bajaria-with-former-disney-exec-peter-rice/, 2026-10-16), which links it to slowing engagement and weaker originals. Sarandos also said later that the business is 'healthy and growing fine' (https://www.webull.com/news/15690084030678016), which is why this is sized small.

findings.finding: Third-party engagement data points down in H2 2026. Nielsen put Netflix's share of US TV time at 7.8% in July, down from 8.3% earlier and a multi-year low, while YouTube hit a record 14.2%. Wells Fargo's base case (Sep 18) has hours on Netflix's top-100 originals down 21% YoY in H2 2026. Members averaged 1.6 hours a day in H1 2026, about 8% below H1 2023 after adjusting for added households.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Engagement is not a reported KPI. The stock fell 14% in September on these notes, not on a print. Netflix argues view hours are not linear to revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock fell 14% in September (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/01/why-netflix-lost-14-in-september/). What is not priced is whether the Q3 letter confirms an engagement decline, now that the What We Watched report is moving to annual. This is a proxy, not a company number.
findings.independence: Separate source: the adwave Nielsen recap (https://adwave.com/resources/most-watched-streaming-service-q3-2026, 2026-09-28) for the YouTube 14.2% July record. It shares a theme with the Sarandos finding but rests on different data, sized so the theme is not counted twice.

findings.finding: The dollar has strengthened since the July FY guide was set, a headwind to Q4 reported revenue. EUR/USD was 1.1444 on 2026-07-15 and is 1.1215 on 2026-10-20 (-2.0%), after a Fed hike on 2026-09-16 lifted the dollar index 2.4% in two weeks. If that holds through Q4, it pushes reported revenue toward or below the low end of the $51.0-51.4bn FY range, by roughly $100-150M on about $7bn of non-USD Q4 revenue. Q3's average EUR/USD of about 1.145-1.15 was at or slightly above the guide rate, so Q3 itself carries no FX drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Netflix guides at prevailing FX and has trimmed reported-dollar revenue guides for FX before. The July 2026 FY range was narrowed, and the stock fell -7.26% on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side models usually mark FX, so part of this is in estimates. But no preview found mentions FX as a Q4 risk; every preview frames the guide around ads and engagement. If priced, previews would flag a sub-$51bn FY revenue risk. This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed.
findings.independence: Cambridge Currencies' dollar index shows 100.98 on 2026-09-25, up 2.4% since 2026-09-09 (https://cambridgecurrencies.com/us-dollar-index-dxy-forecast/). The July guide rate is at https://www.valutafx.com/history/eur-usd-2026-07-16.

findings.finding: Netflix cut about 1,000 jobs (6% of roughly 16,000 staff) on 2026-10-14, mostly in product, tech, legal and HR, with no disclosed severance charge or savings target. The Q4 severance charge sits in operating expenses and the company reports GAAP only. A charge of about $150-300M would take 1-2 points off the implied 27.7% Q4 margin, so the 31.5% FY margin target could print lower 'including restructuring'. The cuts also save cost into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3 2025 a Brazil tax charge took the margin to 28.2% against a 31.5% guide, and the stock fell -10.07% on that print. A one-off margin miss was punished then.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock rose 2.89% on 2026-10-15 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/16/netflix-is-cutting-about-1000-jobs-and-its-content-chief-is-out-days-before-earnings/), so the market read the cuts as margin-protective and has not priced a lowered FY margin headline. The sign is ambiguous: savings argue for a firmer 2027 margin, which is why this is sized near zero.
findings.independence: 247wallst (2026-10-16) confirms no charge has been disclosed. That piece also treats a lowered 31.5% target as the bear trigger.

findings.finding: UCAN revenue growth slowed to 10% in Q2 2026 from 14% in Q1. The letter attributes this to only a partial-quarter effect of the late-March US price increase ($8.99 / $19.99 / $26.99), so Q3 carries the full-quarter effect and UCAN, 43% of revenue, should reaccelerate. This is the main path to a small Q3 revenue beat against $12.86-12.88bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells reported-quarter beats. Q2 2026 EPS beat ($0.80 vs $0.79) and fell -7.26%. Q1 2026 revenue beat its guide ($12.25bn vs $12.16bn) and fell -9.72%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside the company's own Q3 guide of 12% growth, so it is mostly expected. Wire coverage cites 'deceleration in US and Canada' as a worry (https://www.mediaweek.com.au/netflix-cuts-1-000-jobs-as-content-chief-faces-exit-report) without the letter's partial-quarter explanation.
findings.independence: The price increase is documented at https://www.fox29.com/news/netflix-announces-price-increase-for-58m-subscribers. It shares the shareholder letter with the bar.

findings.finding: Ad momentum looks on track or better for the FY $3bn ad target. Netflix closed its 2026 US upfront with nearly double the prior year's commitments (2026-08-11). The ad tier reached more than 250M monthly active viewers (May). The Week-1 NFL game drew 18.5M average US viewers, level with Amazon's opener. Together these support a reaffirmed or raised ad outlook in the letter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $3bn ad target was reaffirmed in July, and S&P noted it sat below analyst expectations. The stock fell -7.26% anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: The upfront was public in August and the stock fell through September, so it is mostly priced. The ad target is the company's own, so this lands inside the guide. Upside comes only if the letter raises the ad number.
findings.independence: NFL viewership comes from a separate source (https://www.tvtechnology.com/platform/streaming/nfl-melbourne-game-scores-18-5-million-u-s-viewers-on-netflix). Needham and Wedbush previews say $3bn is on track (https://www.benzinga.com/markets/large-cap/26/10/62470573/analysts-eye-3-billion-ad-revenue-surge-ahead-of-netflix-earnings).

findings.finding: Positioning is de-risked into the print. The stock is 4% above its 52-week low and 44% below its high. Five sell-side actions cut ratings or targets between Sep 18 and Oct 19. Short interest is low (about 2%, 1.7 days to cover), the 25-delta skew is upside-paid (-2.07) and put/call OI is 0.63. A Q4 guide merely in line with the implied $13.3-13.7bn would clear a lowered bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five of the last six prints were negative (-7.26, -9.72, -2.18, -10.07, -5.10, +1.53). The one large positive, +9.69% in Jan 2025, came off a de-rated setup.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew and the Polymarket odds already say this, so it agrees with the market's own lean and is sized small. It cuts against the name's habit of selling prints.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo and HSBC downgrades (https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/netflix-stock-wells-fargo-hsbc-downgrade-engagement-trends-youtube-competition/). Polymarket odds (https://finbold.com/traders-predict-netflixs-next-direction-after-tomorrows-earnings-release/).

outside_window.finding: Peter Rice takes over as chief content officer on 2026-10-26. Any content-strategy reset or write-downs he brings would land after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans mildly negative (guide risk, FX, engagement) against a mildly upside-paid skew and a de-rated stock near its low. That tension keeps p_up at 45 rather than lower. The name's habit of selling prints keeps it from going to 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy): FX finding is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed; -0.6 to -0.4.
Lesson 5 (proxy vs company number): Nielsen/Wells Fargo engagement is a proxy beside the CEO's own statement; -0.4 to -0.3. The Sarandos finding stays at -0.6.
Lessons 1 and 6 (beats sold, inside guide): UCAN reacceleration is inside the 12% Q3 guide on a name that sold its last beats; +0.3 to +0.15.
Lesson 6 (inside guide): ad momentum supports the company's own reaffirmed $3bn target; +0.4 to +0.25.
Lesson 2 (one-off): restructuring charge filed as one_off with an ambiguous path (lower FY margin print vs 2027 savings); -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (~2%, 1.7 days to cover, not crowded), skew only mildly upside-paid; no change to the negatives. p_up stays 45, abs_move_pct stays 9.5, scaled number unchanged.
